PART I

Item 1. Business

BUSINESS-MARKER Example Corp designs, makes and sells industrial widgets to manufacturers in North America, Europe and Asia. The company was founded in 1950 and is headquartered in New York. It sells through a direct sales force and through a network of independent distributors that serve smaller customers in more than forty countries.

The widget market is competitive. The company competes on product quality, delivery time and the breadth of its catalog. Its main competitors are large diversified industrial groups and a number of smaller regional makers that focus on single product lines or on a single country.

At the end of the fiscal year the company employed about 12,000 people, of whom about 4,000 worked outside the United States. None of its employees in the United States are covered by collective bargaining agreements, and the company considers its relations with employees to be good.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

RISKFACTORS-MARKER The company's results depend on demand from manufacturers, which falls when industrial production slows. A recession in its main markets could reduce sales, lower prices and leave the company with excess factory capacity and inventory that it would need to write down.

The company buys steel, aluminum and electronic parts from a small number of suppliers. A shortage or a sharp rise in the price of these materials could raise costs faster than the company can raise its own prices, which would reduce margins and could delay deliveries to customers.

The company relies on information systems to run its plants and to take orders. A cyberattack or a failure of these systems could stop production, expose customer data and lead to claims, fines and lost business, and the company's insurance may not cover all of these costs.

Item 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments

None.

PART II

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

MDA-MARKER Net sales rose 6 percent in fiscal 2025 to 4.2 billion dollars, mainly because the company sold more widgets in Europe and raised prices on its premium lines. Sales in North America were flat, as lower volumes offset higher prices, and sales in Asia rose 9 percent on new distributor contracts.

Gross margin improved to 38.5 percent from 37.1 percent a year earlier, as lower freight costs and better factory use more than offset higher wages. Operating expenses rose 4 percent, mostly because of higher spending on research and development for the next generation of widgets.

Cash from operations was 610 million dollars, compared with 540 million dollars a year earlier. The company used the cash to pay down 200 million dollars of debt, buy back shares and pay dividends, and it ended the year with 900 million dollars of cash and a new five-year credit line.

Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk

MARKET-RISK-MARKER The company is exposed to changes in interest rates on its floating-rate debt and to changes in foreign exchange rates, mainly the euro and the yen. A one percentage point rise in interest rates would raise annual interest expense by about 3 million dollars on the debt outstanding at year end.

Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data

STATEMENTS-MARKER Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm. To the Board of Directors and Stockholders of Example Corp: we have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Example Corp as of the end of fiscal 2025 and 2024 and the related statements of income, cash flows and stockholders' equity.

Opinion on the Financial Statements

In our opinion, the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the company and the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended at the end of fiscal 2025, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States.

Note 1. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies

The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Example Corp and its subsidiaries. All intercompany balances and transactions are eliminated.
